newsitem.title: Hong kong: HK's Tung to report Beijing on choice of officials.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung to report Beijing on choice of officials.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Monday he would travel to Beijing this week to report to China's leaders on his choice of top officials to serve after Britain hands over the territory this year.
His office said in a statement Tung would "nominate and report to the Central People's government" on Wednesday and return from Beijing on Thursday.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
The departing British colonial administration has urged Tung to make as few changes as possible in the ranks of top civil servants, who hold positions akin to cabinet ministers in Britain.

Tung won public acclaim when he invited Hong Kong's popular Chief Secretary, Anson Chan, head of the civil service and deputy to British Governor Chris Patten, to stay on, guaranteeing a measure of continuity in uncertain times.
She accepted, but the fate of her senior policy secretaries remains to be decided.
The British colonial government said on Monday it had no intention of seconding senior officials to help Tung ahead of the handover on July 1.
The Hong Kong government has already seconded some 30 staff to Tung's office.

Tung said on Sunday after meeting visiting British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind he hoped Britain would agree to second one or two of their top civil servants to his private office before the sovereignty transfer.
Tung named his inner circle of advisers, or Executive Council, last month.
The list included two members who serve on the colonial Governor's Executive Council.
